prompt.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: a FIVE-FRAME SPRITE SHEET of this exact Song dynasty figure (role: 抬运者 · 扶杠搬运; the Chinese caption is for context only, never draw text): one standing pose plus one complete four-frame walk cycle, walking toward the RIGHT of the image. TWO reference images. The FIRST shows the exact character(s) to draw: copy identity, faces, hair, clothing colours, headwear and carried objects from it. Its camera angle may be from behind or from above; IGNORE that angle only. The SECOND reference is a finished walk sheet of a different person: copy ONLY its camera angle (eye-level three-quarter side view, the same as every other figure on the street), its figure scale and its five-cell layout. Do NOT copy that person.  Carried objects stay in the same hands or on the same shoulder or back in every cell. If the figure holds a walking stick or staff, it reaches the ground and swings forward with the opposite leg. IMPORTANT for this figure: the FIRST reference already faces and leans toward the RIGHT; keep her whole body exactly that way round. She walks forward toward the RIGHT: face, chest, leaning torso and leading foot all point RIGHT, and the big burlap sack hangs BEHIND her from the LEFT (rear) end of the carrying pole, trailing behind her back. The sack must never be in front of her. Her upper body and her legs move in the same direction. Cell 1 = standing at rest, facing right. Cell 2 = contact: front leg forward with heel touching the ground, back leg on its toes, longest stride. Cell 3 = passing: weight on the straight supporting leg under the body, the other leg bent and passing forward, foot just off the ground. Cell 4 = contact with the opposite leg forward, mirror of cell 2. Cell 5 = passing with the opposite leg, mirror of cell 3. The head stays at the same height and the same horizontal position in every walking cell; the body only bobs very slightly. Correct leg anatomy, robe and skirt hems swing with the legs, no extra limbs. If the Chinese role caption disagrees with the FIRST reference (for example the reference carries a staff, basket, box or bundle the caption does not mention), follow the reference. Fine ink outlines and muted antique Chinese watercolor exactly matching the first reference, same line weight, same palette, same paper-grain shading. Truly transparent alpha background, no ground shadow, no glow, no grid lines, no numbers, no text. One single horizontal row of 5 equal-width cells, all walking toward the RIGHT of the image, centered in each cell with generous margin so heads, tools, bundles and feet never touch a cell edge. Canvas: one wide landscape image split into exactly 5 invisible equal-width columns. Every part of each figure - farthest stride, staff tip, trailing sleeve, bundle - stays wholly inside its own column with a clear transparent gap of at least one tenth of the column width on both sides; nothing overlaps a neighbouring column. If a pose is too wide, draw the figure smaller in ALL cells rather than let it cross a column line. Identical figure size and identical camera angle in every cell. Redraw at higher detail than the small reference without changing the design. Make every cell match the first reference and match each other as strictly as possible.

label: 抬运者 · 扶杠搬运
note: v1 copied the reference's leftward body (sack trailing on the right) onto rightward legs, so she seemed to walk backwards. v2 uses the mirrored reference.
